# Reflecting telescope (`reflecting_telescope`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/physics.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Physics, optics & astronomy (`physics`)
- Deps: needs telescope; helped by glass_mirrors, copper_bronze
- Core idea: A concave mirror gathers the light instead of a lens, so there are no colour fringes and the instrument can be short and wide. Newton's form: a slightly hollow mirror at the bottom of the tube, a small flat mirror at 45 degrees near the top that throws the image to an eyepiece in the side. The mirror was cast from speculum metal, a white, brittle bronze of roughly two parts copper to one part tin, ground hollow against a convex tool and polished on pitch; it needs repolishing as it tarnishes. For high power the sphere must be deepened to a parabola. From the 1850s a thin layer of silver on glass replaced the metal.
- Pitfalls:
  - Ordinary bronze or a looking-glass mirror will not do (double reflection from glass with a backing)
  - A mirror surface must be about four times as accurate as a lens surface
  - Thinking Newton's first instrument outperformed the refractors of its day (it was a proof of principle)
- History: europe: 1616 Zucchi tries; 1663 James Gregory's design; 1668 Newton builds the first working one; 1721 Hadley's parabolic mirror makes it practical; 1789 William Herschel's 1.2 m; 1856–1857 Steinheil and Foucault, silver on glass
- Read:
  - Isaac Newton, An Accompt of a New Catadioptrical Telescope, Philosophical Transactions 7 (1672)
  - Henry C. King, The History of the Telescope (1955)
